issues.quote: Madame said the master must come down for the toast, so I went up to fetch him.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no event about Madame calling for Monsieur Monnier or about anyone going up to the atelier, and gives no time for it.
issues.misreading: A solver could read this as placing Madame in the house and in contact with Rosa at a particular point, possibly after the piano stopped at 11:01 by the kitchen clock, which is a whereabouts and sequence the sheet does not support.

issues.quote: The old clock in the hall has its own face and its own ways, and I do not touch it.
issues.fact: R4 only states that the hall clock struck eleven when the kitchen clock showed 11:03. The sheet says nothing about the hall clock's accuracy or how it runs.
issues.misreading: The phrase 'its own ways' hints that the hall clock runs fast, slow, or otherwise unreliably, so a solver might discount or re-time the hall-clock strike against the kitchen clock.
